prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. Injury: whiplash. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1247; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, if that's acceptable. You can use the case reference.

Q: The court reporter needs it for the transcript, so I'll ask again. Are you the plaintiff in this matter?

A: Yes, I am the plaintiff.

Q: Thank you. Now, tell me about the collision. Where were you when it happened?

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in League City, Texas, in the right lane. I had been sitting there for maybe thirty seconds when I felt a hard impact from behind.

Q: What were you doing just before you were struck?

A: I was waiting for the light to change. I had my foot on the brake and my hands on the wheel. I wasn't on my phone or looking at anything else.

Q: How would you describe the impact?

A: It was a hard jolt. My head snapped back and then forward, and the seatbelt locked across my chest. The airbags did not deploy, but the car was pushed forward into the intersection.

Q: Did you speak with the other driver at the scene?

A: Yes. He got out and apologized right away. He said he had looked down at his navigation screen and didn't see that traffic had stopped.

Q: When did you first notice pain or stiffness?

A: Within about an hour I had a stiff neck and a headache. By the next morning the pain had spread into my upper back and shoulders, and turning my head to check mirrors was difficult.

Q: Did you seek medical care?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same evening. They took X-rays, told me it looked like whiplash, and gave me a referral to a physical therapist.

Q: Describe your treatment since then.

A: I've been going to physical therapy about three times a week. I also have a prescription for muscle relaxers, and I use a heating pad most nights. My doctor has talked about possibly doing injections if the pain doesn't improve.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: I used to coach my daughter's soccer team on weekends, and I've had to step back from that. I can't lift groceries comfortably, and I've had trouble sleeping because I can't find a position that doesn't hurt. I also stopped going to my weekly volleyball league.

Q: Have you missed any work?

A: I've missed several days, and some days I've worked a reduced schedule because sitting at my desk for long periods makes the pain worse.

Q: Before this collision, had you ever injured your neck or back?

A: No. I had no real problems with my neck or back before this happened.
